title: Learn
description: Learn file processing as data flow: File → Variable/Array → Process → Output/File.

blocks.text: File handling problems are not just about OPENFILE and READFILE. They are about moving data from a file into variables or arrays, processing that data, then outputting or writing the result.

blocks.title: Think of file processing as:
items: File → read data
Variable or array → store data
Processing → count, total, search, filter or compare
Output or another file → show/save result

blocks.title: Common exam tasks:
items: Read all records from a file
Count records
Process numeric data from a file
Search for a record
Read file data into arrays
Filter records and write selected data to another file
Process records with more than one field

slides.title: Read and Output Records
slides.problem: A file called Names.txt stores one name per line. Read and output every name.
slides.code:
DECLARE name : STRING

OPENFILE "Names.txt" FOR READ

WHILE NOT EOF("Names.txt")
    READFILE "Names.txt", name
    OUTPUT name
ENDWHILE

CLOSEFILE "Names.txt"
slides.explanation: Each line is read into the variable name, then immediately output. The EOF loop stops when the file has no more records.

slides.title: Try It
slides.task: A file called Items.txt stores one item name per line. Write pseudocode to read and output every item.
slides.expectedAnswer:
DECLARE item : STRING

OPENFILE "Items.txt" FOR READ

WHILE NOT EOF("Items.txt")
    READFILE "Items.txt", item
    OUTPUT item
ENDWHILE

CLOSEFILE "Items.txt"

markScheme.criterion: DECLARE variable to store each item

blocks.text: Many file questions combine file handling with data processing. After reading each value, you may need to count, total, compare or filter it.

slides.title: Inside the EOF loop you usually:

blocks.title: Inside the EOF loop you usually:
items: READFILE into a variable
Check a condition using IF
Update a counter, total, highest or lowest
Write or output selected records

blocks.text:
WHILE NOT EOF("File.txt")
    READFILE "File.txt", value
    // process value here
ENDWHILE

slides.title: Count Passing Marks from a File
slides.problem: A file called Marks.txt stores one mark per line. Count how many marks are 50 or more.
slides.code:
DECLARE mark, count : INTEGER

count <- 0

OPENFILE "Marks.txt" FOR READ

WHILE NOT EOF("Marks.txt")
    READFILE "Marks.txt", mark

    IF mark >= 50 THEN
        count <- count + 1
    ENDIF
ENDWHILE

CLOSEFILE "Marks.txt"

OUTPUT count
slides.explanation: This combines file processing with counting with condition. READFILE gets the mark, IF checks it, and count tracks how many pass.

slides.title: Try It
slides.task: A file called Sales.txt stores one sales value per line. Write pseudocode to calculate and output the total sales.
slides.expectedAnswer:
DECLARE sale, total : REAL

total <- 0

OPENFILE "Sales.txt" FOR READ

WHILE NOT EOF("Sales.txt")
    READFILE "Sales.txt", sale
    total <- total + sale
ENDWHILE

CLOSEFILE "Sales.txt"

OUTPUT total

blocks.text: Sometimes the data from a file needs to be stored for later use. This is when arrays are useful.
A counter is used as the array index. Each time a record is read, the counter increases and the value is stored in the next array position.

slides.title: Reading File Data into Arrays: Code pattern

blocks.text:
count <- 0

WHILE NOT EOF("File.txt")
    count <- count + 1
    READFILE "File.txt", Values[count]
ENDWHILE

slides.title: Read Names into an Array
slides.problem: A file called Names.txt stores up to 100 names. Read the names into an array.
slides.code:
DECLARE Names : ARRAY[1:100] OF STRING
DECLARE count : INTEGER

count <- 0

OPENFILE "Names.txt" FOR READ

WHILE NOT EOF("Names.txt")
    count <- count + 1
    READFILE "Names.txt", Names[count]
ENDWHILE

CLOSEFILE "Names.txt"
slides.explanation: count tracks how many records have been read and also points to the next array position.

slides.title: Try It
slides.task: A file called Scores.txt stores up to 50 scores. Write pseudocode to read the scores into an array called Scores.

blocks.text: Some questions require writing to a file. This may be writing new data, or reading from one file and writing selected records to another file.

slides.title: When filtering to a new file:

blocks.title: When filtering to a new file:
items: Open the input file for READ
Open the output file for WRITE
Read each record from the input file
Use IF to check whether the record should be saved
WRITEFILE only the selected records
Close both files

slides.title: Writing and Filtering File Data: Code pattern

blocks.text:
OPENFILE "Input.txt" FOR READ
OPENFILE "Output.txt" FOR WRITE

WHILE NOT EOF("Input.txt")
    READFILE "Input.txt", value
    IF condition THEN
        WRITEFILE "Output.txt", value
    ENDIF
ENDWHILE

CLOSEFILE "Input.txt"
CLOSEFILE "Output.txt"

slides.title: Write Passing Marks to a New File
slides.problem: Marks.txt stores one mark per line. Write all marks 50 or above to Pass.txt.
slides.code:
DECLARE mark : INTEGER

OPENFILE "Marks.txt" FOR READ
OPENFILE "Pass.txt" FOR WRITE

WHILE NOT EOF("Marks.txt")
    READFILE "Marks.txt", mark

    IF mark >= 50 THEN
        WRITEFILE "Pass.txt", mark
    ENDIF
ENDWHILE

CLOSEFILE "Marks.txt"
CLOSEFILE "Pass.txt"
slides.explanation: This is a filter-write pattern. Only marks meeting the condition are written to the output file.

slides.title: Try It
slides.task: A file called Temperatures.txt stores one temperature per line. Write all temperatures greater than 30 to HotDays.txt.
slides.expectedAnswer:
DECLARE temperature : REAL

OPENFILE "Temperatures.txt" FOR READ
OPENFILE "HotDays.txt" FOR WRITE

WHILE NOT EOF("Temperatures.txt")
    READFILE "Temperatures.txt", temperature

    IF temperature > 30 THEN
        WRITEFILE "HotDays.txt", temperature
    ENDIF
ENDWHILE

CLOSEFILE "Temperatures.txt"
CLOSEFILE "HotDays.txt"
